why: Both moved the single reply call with live verification and both proposed sensible Router guardrails, but B found the two things that decide this app: the {date}/{time} lines sitting at the front of the system prompt destroy the cacheable prefix on every call (fixed in code, conservatively, with the translated body dumped to prove the ordering survives), and the Dockerfile copied only llmcord.py, so the README's documented container deploy would silently never route. That first finding also undercuts A's competing cache item — A sets prompt_cache_key for the feature and quotes bench numbers for it while never noticing that this app's own prompt begins with a clock, so the claimed savings would not land here.
A_best: Caught that llmcord gates image attachments by substring-matching VISION_MODEL_TAGS, so the cheapest catalog id (gpt-6-luna) would silently stop accepting attachments — and used that to pick gpt-5.6-luna instead, shipped as a tested branch; also fixed the per-message AsyncOpenAI client/connection-pool churn and asserted the embed turns green, which is the app's own proof that finish_reason survives the Chat->Responses translation.
B_best: Identified the clock at the head of the system prompt as the reason prompt caching never pays in this app — the largest cost lever given 'resend the whole 25-message chain every turn' — and fixed it with a conservative line-level split verified in the translated request body, alongside catching the Dockerfile gap that would have left the documented deploy unrouted.
A_worst: Its caching story is wrong for this app (both i2's $feature key and i7's per-conversation key assume a stable prefix that the {date}/{time} system prompt breaks every call), and it left the Dockerfile untouched, so the container deploy the README documents would import no runtime and never route.
B_worst: m1 claims 'loses: nothing' when a Chat->Responses translation layer was inserted into a streaming path a human watches — A disclosed that honestly — and the three policy branches each create router.policy.json with no 'excludes' between them, so i1/i2/i3 collide on apply with only a prose note in i3.
